ENT CLINICAL NOTE

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure:
  • Dry, itchy, red skin rash on arms and hands.  
  • Onset a few days ago, noticed after a swimming session; patient also under work-related stress.
- Symptom timeline and progression:
  • Began a few days ago; persistent; no spread beyond arms/hands.
- ENT symptoms:
  • Denies throat swelling/closure sensation, voice change, dysphagia/odynophagia, drooling.  
  • Denies nasal or ocular symptoms, stridor/noisy breathing, dyspnea.  
  • No facial, lip, tongue, or uvular swelling.  
  • No ear pain/hearing changes or neck pain/swelling.
- Relevant past episodes and treatments:
  • No prior similar skin or allergic episodes reported.  
  • No previous ED visits or injection therapy for allergy.
- Allergies and current medications:
  • Possible lactose intolerance (self-reported).  
  • Microgynon (combined oral contraceptive pill) – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
  • Topical coconut butter (self-administered) – dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Social context:
  • Lives alone; works as a primary school teacher; reports significant job stress.

Objective:
- Observable swelling and distribution:
  • Patient verbally reports erythematous, dry, itchy rash on arms/hands; no swelling noted elsewhere.
- Airway/breathing:
  • No reported or observed airway compromise; breathing normal by history.
- Mental status/associated features:
  • No dizziness, syncope, or systemic symptoms.
- Vitals/exam:
  • Not recorded.
- Accompaniment:
  • Patient alone during consultation (remote).

Assessment:
- Likely irritant or contact dermatitis of arms/hands, temporally associated with recent swimming pool exposure; no evidence of acute allergic reaction or airway involvement.

Plan:
- Medications/advice:
  • Prescribe topical steroid cream (specific agent/dose not documented).  
  • Recommend liberal use of emollients.  
  • Over-the-counter non-sedating antihistamine (e.g., loratadine) suggested for pruritus – dose not documented.
- Instructions:
  • Apply emollient frequently throughout the day; use steroid cream as directed.  
  • Avoid identified irritants (e.g., chlorinated pool water) until symptoms resolve.  
  • Monitor for red-flag symptoms: throat tightness, voice change, breathing difficulty, facial/lip/tongue swelling, rapid rash progression; seek urgent medical help (call emergency number) if any occur.
- Follow-up:
  • Review in one week if no improvement or sooner if symptoms worsen.  
  • Provide patient information leaflet on dermatitis.

Quality checks (document_quality):
● Missing/expected elements:
  – Formal allergy list beyond “possible lactose intolerance.”  
  – Inquiry about auto-injector ownership or prior anaphylaxis plan (reasonable but not performed).  
  – Detailed ENT/airway physical examination and vitals.  
  – Exact steroid preparation, potency, and dosing instructions.
● Internal conflicts: none noted.
● Transcript quality: clear overall; occasional inaudible segments and minor omissions, but key clinical details discernible.
